page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.1-2 is an Arm-based virtual machine instance within the Standard family. It is powered by an Ampere Altra processor operating at a base frequency of 3.0 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 1 dedicated physical core mapped to 1 vCPU, featuring single-threaded execution per core without hyper-threading. The allocation provides consistent compute cycles without the thread contention common in multi-tenant shared-core architectures.

The instance is configured with 2.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It includes no bundled local NVMe storage, meaning all disk persistence relies on attached network block volumes. It provides one complimentary public IPv4 address for ingress and egress networking, while lacking hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

Due to the lightweight resource allocation of 1 vCPU and 2.0 GB of RAM on an efficient Arm Neoverse-based platform, this profile provides high cost efficiency for entry-level tasks. However, the 2.0 GB memory ceiling restricts memory-intensive runtimes, complex multi-tier container stacks, or intensive data transformations.

VM.Standard.A1.Flex.1-2 is suitable for low-footprint Linux workloads, basic web serving, lightweight microservices, testing environments, network proxy forwarding, and development sandboxes designed for the 64-bit Arm architecture.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.1-2 is an entry-level compute instance powered by a 3.0 GHz Ampere Altra Arm processor. The configuration includes 1 dedicated vCPU backed by 1 physical core with 1 thread per core, paired with 2.0 GB of system memory. The instance features no local storage and relies on network-attached block storage, while including 1 complimentary public IPv4 address and omitting GPU accelerators. With its 1:2 core-to-memory ratio, the configuration is cost-efficient for lightweight baseline workloads that require dedicated processing without the overhead of shared burstable cores. VM.Standard.A1.Flex.1-2 is designed for lightweight web serving, microservices, utility tasks, development environments, and software compilation targeting the arm64 architecture.
